html:
The Cayuse are a Native American people of the Columbia Plateau, from the Blue Mountains of northeastern Oregon and southeastern Washington.

They were famous horse breeders, and in English "cayuse" came to mean a hardy pony. Their language is almost lost; most Cayuse also spoke the Sahaptin of their neighbours the Nez Perce and Umatilla. They fished salmon and dug roots in the rivers and meadows.

In 1836 the missionary Marcus Whitman set up a mission among them, on the route of the Oregon Trail. In 1847 a measles epidemic brought by migrants killed about half the Cayuse while white children recovered, and some Cayuse killed Whitman and others in the Whitman massacre. The Cayuse War followed. In 1855 the Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla were placed together on the Umatilla Reservation, where their confederated tribes live today.
sum: The Cayuse are a Native American people of the Columbia Plateau, from the Blue Mountains of northeastern Oregon and southeastern Washington.
